verdict: ROAS dropped sharply this week; purchases are clustering, not converting steadily.
narrative: Return on ad spend fell 63% week-over-week to 3.56, on $1,509 in Meta spend over the last 28 days — and the decline is accelerating, with only 2 purchases recorded in the last three days versus 6 in the three days prior. The core issue is purchase clustering: sales are arriving in bursts on isolated days, with zero purchases on 8 of the last 10 days, which signals that current creative is not driving a reliable conversion rhythm at this spend level. At the same time, Instagram reach has dropped 45% over the past four weeks and Google Business Profile engagement fell 44% week-over-week, pointing to softening demand across both paid and organic touchpoints. Fresh ad creative is being prioritised to address fatigue, and the funnel test and UTM tracking are on track to close by August 31, which will sharpen visibility into what is and isn't converting. Expect cleaner purchase data and updated creative in market before the next report.

highlights.phrase: Return on ad spend in the last 28 days, down 63% from the prior week
Total purchases driven by Meta ads this period, heavily concentrated on just a few days
Google Business Profile actions recorded this period (calls, directions, and site clicks)

watch_item.issue: Purchase volume is collapsing toward near-zero on most days, driven by creative fatigue as existing ads lose effectiveness.
watch_item.fix: New ad creative is being prioritised for immediate production — the overdue live-cooking content shoot is being rescheduled to unblock the fresh creative pipeline.
